opening.argument: The recording shows a drawing process, not proof of deception. A Facebook post displays a purported $500 Lowe's gift card and a numbered participant list; the stated arrangement is $50 per spot. The speaker walks through dice rolls and repeated list randomization before announcing a selection. Those steps document how the drawing was presented. They do not establish whether the card was valid, whether anyone paid or received it, or whether there was false delivery, theft, or victim loss. The visible selection cannot, by itself, prove either a completed transaction or a deceptive one.
